chunks: And as for what Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Muhammad ibn Isma'il from Durust al-Wasiti from 'Ajlan Abu Salih who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), saying: 'A woman performing Hajj al-Tamattu' arrived in Mecca and saw blood (menstruation).' He said: 'She performs Tawaf between As-Safa and Al-Marwah, then sits in her house. If she becomes pure, she performs Tawaf with the House. If she does not become pure, then when it is the Day of Tarwiyah, she pours water over herself, enters the state of Ihram for Hajj from her house, and goes out to Mina, completing all the rituals. When she arrives in Mecca, she performs two Tawafs with the House and performs Sa'i between As-Safa and Al-Marwah. When she does that, everything becomes permissible for her except the marital bed of her husband.'

key_terms.حَجُّ التَّمَتُّعِ: Hajj al-Tamattu' (a type of Hajj where one performs Umrah first, then Hajj)
key_terms.طَوَافُ الْإِفَاضَةِ: Tawaf al-Ifadah (the principal Tawaf of Hajj)
key_terms.يَوْمُ التَّرْوِيَةِ: The Day of Tarwiyah (8th of Dhu al-Hijjah)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling for a woman who gets her period during Hajj al-Tamattu' before completing the final Tawaf?
ai.summary: This narration from Shaykh al-Tusi’s *Tahdhib* details the specific fiqh for a woman in Hajj al-Tamattu' who menstruates before Tawaf al-Ifadah, instructing her to delay the final Tawaf and Sa'i until purity is regained while completing other rites in Mina. It highlights the Shia juristic view that marital relations remain prohibited until the completion of both Tawaf and Sa'i, distinguishing this from the Hanafi view which often considers Tawaf alone sufficient for full release. The hadith underscores the practical flexibility of delaying the final pillar without invalidating the Hajj, provided the woman remains in a state of Ihram or performs the necessary compensatory acts.
